1.8 A read-only check changes the closed catalog’s sidecars

Symptom. A later closed-catalog check refuses a new WAL/SHM family even though the Main file identity is unchanged. A read-only SQLite connection can still participate in WAL bookkeeping. Checking only the preparation reader can miss readers inside worker preflight, current-row validation or alias queries.

Prerequisites. Establish actual normal Classic closure, settle its helpers, and retain the operation’s process/descriptor observations and resource owner. Bind the Main identity, companion state, permitted jobs and a finite reader lifetime. An absent process or an empty WAL alone does not establish this boundary.

Procedure. In a qualified closed-catalog workflow, route every Main query through the same bounded immutable reader contract. Keep indexed query-plan, row-cardinality, argument/job, before/after identity and close-ownership checks. Use mode=ro&immutable=1 only when that contract establishes a stable database and accounts for its WAL state. SQLite documents that immutable mode omits locking and change detection; a changing file can yield incorrect results. SQLite URI parameters.

Verify. Exercise the actual emitted worker reader expressions against a disposable database with the production job parser. Verify that no sidecars appear and that stale gates and substituted jobs refuse before querying. Then verify a real publication followed by its next closed-epoch continuation. Source tests alone do not qualify that native sequence.

Undo. Preserve the original refusal and successful earlier publications. Do not remove WAL/SHM files or rewrite the expected state to make a check pass. Resolve uncertain owners first; obtain a fresh normal lifecycle boundary when needed and issue a distinct request. Do not repeat a pending native operation.

Limits. This is not an immutable-read recipe for an open or changing catalog. It does not authorize ignoring committed WAL frames, externally writing Main, or treating a known read-only sidecar change as proof of broader integrity.
